newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says Italy "solemnly committed" to EMU.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy "solemnly committed" to EMU.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Wednesday that Italy was "solemnly committed" to meeting the economic conditions for membership from the outset in 1999 of Europe's planned Monetary and Economic Union (EMU).

He issued a statement rejecting reports that Italy could be offered a deal to delay its entry to the single currency as false, unjustified and unfounded. "They do nothing but generate uncertainty among Italians and on financial markets," he said.

Prodi issued his statement after the Financial Times nespaper said Italy would be offered a deal that would delay its entry into EMU until 2000 or 2001 to assuage German fears that initial lira entry would weaken the single currency.
The newspaper, quoting unnamed senior monetary officials, described the deal as "a face-saving compromise designed by senior European central bankers and monetary officials".

"Prime Minister Romano Prodi...reaffirms Italy's firm intention and solemn commitment to meet the convergence criteria envisaged under the Maastricht Treaty within the time foreseen," the official statement said.
"The Italian government...deplores the constant repetition of false stories and unjustified statements, including from authoritative media, which have no foundation whatsoever," the statement said.
